Surface.description: Shared background geometry. Layout, spacing between children and behavior belong to consumers.

props.name: padding
props.description: Omit for responsive padding; 0 removes padding.

props.name: density
props.description: compact gives the controls inside the compact control height, which still grows for touch.

props.name: render
props.description: Compose another component onto the same root. It must forward native props and refs.

Table.Body.description: The data rows of a table, a native tbody, separated by hairlines.

Table.Cell.description: A data cell, a native td, with a label that names its value while rows stack.

props.name: label
props.description: The column's name, shown before the value while a table with narrowLayout="stack" stacks its rows. Assistive technology reads the column header instead.

props.name: align
props.description: Aligns the content with the start or the end of the cell.

props.name: numeric
props.description: Tabular figures aligned to the end, for numbers that compare down a column. In a sortable header the arrow comes before the label, so the label lines up with the numbers.

props.name: nowrap
props.description: Keeps the content on one line. In a table with set column widths, content that doesn't fit ends with an ellipsis.

Table.Head.description: The header rows of a table, a native thead, which hold the column headers.

Table.HeaderCell.description: A header cell, a native th that heads its column, or its row with scope="row". With onSort it sorts its column; in a table with resizable columns it holds the column's resize handle.

props.name: sortDirection
props.description: The column's sort order: aria-sort on the header and the arrow in its sort button. Use it with onSort; without onSort it only sets aria-sort.

props.name: onSort
props.description: The header becomes a button across the cell that asks the application to sort the rows by this column. The application sorts the rows and sets sortDirection.

props.name: sortLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the sort button, which says what pressing it does: the header's name followed by "sort ascending", or by "sort descending" while the column is sorted ascending.

props.name: resizeLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the column's resize handle, "Resize" followed by the header's name.

props.name: align
props.description: Aligns the content with the start or the end of the cell.

props.name: numeric
props.description: Tabular figures aligned to the end, for numbers that compare down a column. In a sortable header the arrow comes before the label, so the label lines up with the numbers.

props.name: nowrap
props.description: Keeps the content on one line. In a table with set column widths, content that doesn't fit ends with an ellipsis.

Table.Root.description: A semantic data table on a rounded surface, in a focusable region that scrolls sideways when the columns do not fit.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name of the table and its scroll region when there is no caption. A table needs a caption or an aria-label.

props.name: caption
props.description: A visible caption above the rows that names the table and its scroll region, in place of aria-label. Under a sticky header it scrolls away with the rows.

props.name: density
props.description: standard rows, or compact rows with smaller text and padding for dense data. Buttons, icon buttons and fields in compact cells take the 2 rem compact control height.

props.name: stickyHeader
props.description: The header row stays at the top of the region while the rows scroll beneath it. The region then scrolls vertically too, so give it a height through regionClassName or the surrounding layout.

props.name: regionClassName
props.description: Class of the scroll region around the table, for example to limit its height.

props.name: narrowLayout
props.description: What the table does when its region is narrower than stackBelow: scroll keeps the columns and scrolls sideways; stack shows each body row as a block that starts with its first cell, followed by the other cells with their labels. The header row is then visually hidden.

props.name: stackBelow
props.description: The region width below which a table with narrowLayout="stack" stacks its rows: a CSS length such as 60rem or 480px, or a number of pixels, such as 600 or "600". Wide tables, such as seven sortable columns, need more.

props.name: onStackedChange
props.description: Called with true when the rows stack and with false when the columns return, from the same measurement as stackBelow, for example to show another sort control while the header row is hidden; a table that leaves while its rows stack reports false. The region has data-stacked while the rows stack.

props.name: columnWidths
props.description: Column widths in percent of the table width, in column order and adding up to 100, for widths the application controls with onColumnWidthsChange. Set widths fix the columns: long words wrap and nowrap cells end with an ellipsis.

props.name: defaultColumnWidths
props.description: Starting column widths, in percent, when the table owns them; other defaults start them over. Double-clicking a resize handle restores them, or else the widths a controlled table started with.

props.name: onColumnWidthsChange
props.description: Called with every column's width when people resize a column.

props.name: minColumnWidths
props.description: Smallest width of each column in percent, in column order, or one value for every column.

props.name: resizableColumns
props.description: People can resize the columns with a handle at the end of each header cell but the last, which moves the boundary to the next column and keeps the table's width. Needs columnWidths or defaultColumnWidths.

Table.Row.description: A row of a table, a native tr, which can highlight on hover or be selected.

props.name: interactive
props.description: The row highlights on hover and while focus is inside it, for rows that open something through a link or button in a cell. It adds no behavior of its own.

props.name: selected
props.description: The row is selected: it reports aria-selected and takes the selection colors, with a bar at its start. Pass false to the other rows of a table whose rows can be selected; unset, a row reports no selection state.

Tabs.description: Linked tab panels; supplied buttons retain their own colors, geometry and behavior.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name of the tab list.

props.name: activation
props.description: Automatic selection on arrow-key focus; manual requires Enter or Space.

props.name: keepMounted
props.description: Preserve local panel state while inactive. Hidden panels are inert.

props.name: renderList
props.description: Wrap the supplied list in a custom layout, such as a Card with a heading. Render it once.

props.name: fill
props.description: The selected panel takes the height left below the list; give the Tabs a height (for example as a flex child). For content that fills a region, such as a canvas.

props.name: size
props.description: standard (default) matches buttons; compact makes the whole rail as tall as a compact control, for toolbars and bars, like a compact `SegmentedControl`.

Text.description: Semantic native text with typography and color from the shared token scale.

TextField.description: A labelled single-line text input: a native input with a floating label, a hint and an error, in an outlined, plain or quiet look, with an optional start icon, end action, prefix and suffix.

props.name: label
props.description: The field's visible name, such as Project name; it also names the control for assistive technology.

props.name: hint
props.description: Lasting guidance under the field, such as a format or a limit, linked to the control as its description.

props.name: error
props.description: A message under the field that says how to correct the value. While it is set, the control is invalid (aria-invalid) and the message joins its description, after the hint.

props.name: variant
props.description: The field's look: outlined, with a thin border; plain, with no border or fill and an underline on hover and focus; or quiet, only its text and start icon at rest, with a soft fill under the pointer and while focused and a placeholder that clears on focus, for a search at the top of a sidebar or a list.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: A decorative icon at the start of the field, such as Search or Mail.

props.name: endAction
props.description: A control at the end of the field, such as a text IconButton that reveals or copies the value; name it with aria-label.

props.name: compact
props.description: Take the shared control height and a pill shape, to sit beside buttons in a toolbar. The label is hidden unless showLabel is set; it still names the field for assistive technology, and a placeholder gives the visible guidance.

props.name: showLabel
props.description: Show the label in the field, where it rests while the field is empty and floats into the outline while the field has focus or a value. Compact fields hide it unless this is set.

props.name: prefix
props.description: Short, non-interactive text before the value, such as the start of an address. It is not part of the value; it shows once the field has focus or a value and is read after the label.

props.name: suffix
props.description: Short, non-interactive text after the value, such as a unit. It is not part of the value; it shows once the field has focus or a value and is read after the label.

Textarea.description: A labelled text area for text over several lines: a native textarea in the text field's frame, at a fixed height that scrolls and resizes from its bottom edge, or growing with its content.

props.name: sizing
props.description: How the height follows the text: fixed keeps its height, scrolls and resizes from the bottom edge, by dragging it or with the arrow keys; content grows and shrinks with the text.

props.name: rows
props.description: The lines the field shows: with fixed sizing, its height in rows, at least 7.5 rem; with content sizing, the lines it starts at and shrinks back to, also under 7.5 rem. Without rows, both start at 7.5 rem.

props.name: label
props.description: The field's visible name, such as Project name; it also names the control for assistive technology.

props.name: hint
props.description: Lasting guidance under the field, such as a format or a limit, linked to the control as its description.

props.name: error
props.description: A message under the field that says how to correct the value. While it is set, the control is invalid (aria-invalid) and the message joins its description, after the hint.

props.name: variant
props.description: The field's look: outlined, with a thin border; plain, with no border or fill and an underline on hover and focus; or quiet, only its text and start icon at rest, with a soft fill under the pointer and while focused and a placeholder that clears on focus, for a search at the top of a sidebar or a list.

Theme.description: An explicit, scoped theme. Theme preference and persistence belong to the app.

ThemePreferenceProvider.description: Owns the theme preference: persistence, the system theme and document-root theming.

props.name: storageKey
props.description: localStorage key; match the bootstrap script's. Defaults to "env-theme".

props.name: defaultPreference
props.description: Used when nothing is stored. Defaults to "system".

props.name: applyToDocument
props.description: Theme the document root as well as this subtree (default). Root theming covers the page background, native controls, portals rendered by other libraries and the content of every theme-color meta tag, which takes the canvas color.

props.name: className
props.description: Class name for the Theme boundary around the children.

ThemeToggle.description: Switches between the light and dark themes and stores the choice.

props.name: variant
props.description: As Button's; secondary by default.

props.name: pending
props.description: As Button's: a spinner replaces the icon while the work runs.

TitleBar.description: A window title bar without the application shell, for a start page or a simple window of an installed web app or desktop shell that draws its own title bar. It looks like AppShell's title bar: empty space drags the window, it leaves room for the window controls the system draws, and controls inside are compact. It is a normal block; WindowFrame puts it above content that scrolls on its own.

props.name: start
props.description: Content at the inline start, such as the application mark and a Menubar.

props.name: children
props.description: Content centered in the bar, such as the document title.

props.name: end
props.description: Content at the inline end, such as actions; the window controls follow it.

Toast.Provider.description: Hosts the managed notifications that useToast shows, in a region per placement.

props.name: visibleLimit
props.description: Maximum visible per placement (default 3). Newest notices stay visible; older ones hide behind a count.

Tooltip.description: A small label that describes a control on hover and keyboard focus.

props.name: content
props.description: Short supplementary text; never the only place essential information appears.

props.name: children
props.description: The described control. A disabled control is wrapped so it can still be focused and hovered.

props.name: side
props.description: top (default), bottom, left, right, or inline-start and inline-end, which follow the text direction.

props.name: delay
props.description: Milliseconds before the tooltip opens on hover; focus opens it immediately. Defaults to 400.

Tree.description: A virtualized tree of rows for large hierarchies such as file trees. The application passes the visible rows and owns expansion; the tree owns focus, keyboard navigation and scrolling.

props.name: items
props.description: The visible rows in order, flattened; the application owns expansion.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible name of the tree.

props.name: selectedId
props.description: The selected row; it scrolls into view when it changes.

props.name: onOpen
props.description: Click and Space call it with preview true; double click and Enter with preview false.

props.name: onExpandedChange
props.description: Chevron clicks, ArrowRight on a collapsed row and ArrowLeft on an expanded row.

props.name: contextMenu
props.description: Menu items for a row, or for the tree's empty area when the item is null.

props.name: contextMenuLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the context menu.

props.name: density
props.description: compact (default) rows are about 1.75 rem tall, with a compact context menu; standard rows about 2.25 rem.

WindowFrame.description: A window without the application shell, such as a start page: it fills the window with the title bar on top and the content scrolling below it, so the window controls drawn over the title bar never cover a scrollbar. The keyboard scrolls the content as it would the document.

props.name: titleBar
props.description: The window's title bar at the top, typically a TitleBar.

props.name: children
props.description: The window's content, which scrolls below the title bar.

props.name: scrollRef
props.description: The element that scrolls the content, to read and restore scroll positions.

countDiffLines.description: How many lines a change adds and removes, as a DiffStat shows them.
countDiffLines.signature: (before: string, after: string, filename?: string): { additions: number; deletions: number; }

createRichTextExtensions.description: Shared schema for editing, Markdown IO, and static rendering. Custom extensions append.

createThemeBootstrapScript.description: Inline script for the document head. It themes the root element before the first paint, so a saved or system dark theme does not flash light while the application loads.

formatRelativeTime.description: A moment as text relative to another, by default the current time, such as "in 2 days", "3 hours ago" or "just now", through Intl.RelativeTimeFormat. An invalid moment gives an empty string; an invalid now is ignored, as by RelativeTime, for the current time.

useAppShell.description: Shell controls for content rendered inside AppShell.

useTheme.description: Returns the originating theme, including across React portals.

useThemePreference.description: The theme preference from the nearest ThemePreferenceProvider.

useToast.description: Shows and dismisses notifications through the nearest Toast.Provider.
